[Thinking]
**Creating a study plan**

Alright, it seems like I need to put together a study plan or to-do list. I should think through what subjects or topics need attention and prioritize them. It might help to break everything down into manageable tasks and set some deadlines. I wonder if I should also consider different study methods for each subject? Let’s see how I can organize it all to make sure it’s effective and helps reach those study goals!
[/Thinking]

Absolutely — here’s a practical **NCLEX pass checklist / to-do list** you can follow.

## NCLEX To-Do List

### 1) Set your test date
- Pick a realistic exam date
- Create a study calendar counting backward from test day

### 2) Gather your study materials
- One main NCLEX review book
- One question bank
- Notes or flashcards
- NCLEX test plan/patient safety priorities outline

### 3) Take a baseline practice test
- Do a full-length diagnostic exam
- Identify weak areas
- Track your score so you can measure improvement

### 4) Make a weekly study plan
- Set daily study goals
- Focus more time on weak subjects
- Include review, practice questions, and rationales

### 5) Master the high-yield topics
Study these first:
- Safety and infection control
- Prioritization and delegation
- Pharmacology
- Basic care and comfort
- Physiological adaptation
- Health promotion and maintenance
- Psychosocial integrity

### 6) Practice questions every day
- Aim for 75–150 questions daily if possible
- Review every rationale, even for correct answers
- Learn why wrong answers are wrong

### 7) Work on test-taking strategy
- Answer the question being asked
- Eliminate obviously wrong options
- Prioritize unstable, acute, or critical patients
- Remember: airway, breathing, circulation first

### 8) Review nursing fundamentals
- Vital signs
- Isolation precautions
- Wound care
- Fluid and electrolytes
- IV therapy
- Documentation
- Delegation rules

### 9) Memorize key lab values and medications
- Normal lab ranges
- Critical lab values
- Common drug classes and side effects
- Antidotes and adverse reactions

### 10) Study ATI/NCLEX-style frameworks
- ABCs
- Maslow’s hierarchy
- Nursing process
- Least restrictive/least invasive approach
- Acute vs chronic
- Stable vs unstable

### 11) Practice alternate-format questions
- SATA
- Priority
- Ordered response
- Chart/exhibit questions
- Pharmacology calculations

### 12) Take timed practice exams
- Simulate test conditions
- Practice endurance
- Work on pacing and focus

### 13) Review weak areas repeatedly
- Go back to topics you keep missing
- Relearn before moving on
- Keep an error log of missed questions

### 14) Learn delegation and scope of practice
- Know what can be assigned to UAP, LPN/LVN, and RN
- Focus on what requires RN judgment

### 15) Prepare your test-day routine
- Know the testing center location
- Pack required ID
- Sleep well the night before
- Eat a balanced meal
- Arrive early

### 16) Stay mentally steady
- Take breaks during studying
- Avoid cramming the night before
- Use positive self-talk
- Build confidence with repeated practice

---

## Simple Daily NCLEX Study Template
- **30 min** content review
- **1–2 hours** practice questions
- **30 min** rationale review
- **15 min** flashcards or weak-topic review

---

## Final Week To-Do
- Do 1–2 full-length practice exams
- Review your weakest 3 topics
- Revisit lab values, meds, and prioritization
- Light review only the day before
- Rest and sleep

If you want, I can also make you:
1. a **30-day NCLEX study plan**,  
2. a **daily checklist**, or  
3. a **priority list of the most tested NCLEX topics**.
